warp.guard: Warp's default execution profile auto-approves commands, code diffs, MCP and child agents with an empty denylist. The ExecutionProfiles preference is cloud-synced: a local settings.toml denylist was overwritten on the next launch, and the Oz log reports 'Attempted to edit CLI default profile, which is not yet supported.' The dispatcher therefore guards through the child environment: GIT_CONFIG_* rewrites https://, git@ and ssh:// push URLs to an unhandled scheme, GH_CONFIG_DIR points at an empty directory, and GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are removed. Verified on a scratch repo: push aborts, fetch URL unchanged, gh reports not logged in. Not guarded: local destructive commands and other cloud CLIs (railway, az, doctl); run Warp only in C:\wt worktrees. settings.toml agents.warp_agent.other.auto_approve_bypasses_command_denylist = false (backup settings.toml.bak-agenthub-peer-20261026).

hostSurfaces.purpose: A host is not one uniform capability target. Codex CLI, the Codex IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app are the same registered host reading the same ~/.codex config, but they do NOT expose the same tools -- routing a task to the built-in Browser succeeds on one and silently has nowhere to go on another. This records which surface actually offers which capability, so a skill can request an outcome and resolve a provider instead of naming a tool that may not exist where it runs.
hostSurfaces.modelNote: Deliberately NOT modelled as extra entries in registry/agents.json. Hosts are split there when their surfaces read DIFFERENT paths -- antigravity-ide and cursor-agent each have their own config file, which is what earns them a host entry. Every Claude surface reads ~/.claude and every Codex surface reads ~/.codex, so splitting them would duplicate 11 and 12 capability mappings that deploy to identical destinations and add nothing. What differs is capability availability, and that lives here.

capabilityMeanings.browser.isolated: A browser the agent drives itself with a throwaway or per-workspace profile, carrying no signed-in session. Suits localhost and public pages. This is the capability that scales across hosts, because no two sessions contend for one profile directory -- Playwright MCP partitions automatically as mcp-{channel}-{workspace-hash}, and --isolated removes the on-disk profile entirely.
capabilityMeanings.browser.authenticated: A browser carrying a signed-in session, so already-authenticated sites work without logging in each run. Owner direction 2026-10-23: Codex, Cursor and Claude use their native browser surface. Hosts without a native browser pane use Playwright MCP --extension through browser-toolkit when needed, never persisted as session-start stdio. Chrome DevTools MCP is retired across the fleet.
capabilityMeanings.computer.gui: First-party control of native desktop applications.
capabilityMeanings.mobile.android.local: Driving an Android emulator or attached device on the Windows host. On this fleet the provider is the appium-mobile MCP through its embedded UiAutomator2. Does not cover a physical iPhone or any real-hardware claim.
capabilityMeanings.mobile.ios.simulated: Driving an iOS Simulator inside the VMware macOS guest, reached as a remote Appium client because Xcode and simctl do not exist on Windows. On this fleet the provider is the appium-mobile MCP with remoteServerUrl set to the guest. Does not cover a physical iPhone or any real-hardware claim.

hostSurfaces.note: null means not established, never 'assumed false'. Every true and every false must carry its own sentence under this surface's capabilityEvidence, keyed by the capability it backs -- one shared paragraph cannot answer for three capabilities, which is how a false about GUI control once rode on evidence that only discussed browsers. A null carries no writing cost at all: registry/mcps.json requires a null protocol revision to say why, and this table deliberately does not, because charging the honest value a cost that false does not pay is the incentive being inverted here. A capabilityNotEstablished entry is optional, is never read as evidence, and must name a capability this surface still records as null. Enforced by tests/Test-HostSurfaces.ps1.
